cases.sentence: И как бы по волшебству, без мысли о ней ___ правильная и отчетливая делалась сама собой.
cases.translation: And as if by magic, without a thought about it, the work, correct and precise, was done by itself.
cases.explain: Работа is the grammatical subject of the verb делалась (was being done), so it is in the nominative case.

cases.translation: A hen quail flew out from right under the scythe.
cases.explain: The compound preposition из-под (from under) governs the genitive case.

cases.sentence: Еще радостнее были минуты, когда, подходя к ___, в которую утыкались ряды, старик обтирал косу.
cases.translation: Still happier were the moments when, approaching the river into which the rows ran, the old man wiped his scythe clean.
cases.explain: The preposition к (toward) governs the dative case.

cases.sentence: Приходила кочка, он изменял ___, и подбивал ее с обеих сторон короткими ударами.
cases.translation: A hummock would come along; he would change his movement, and trim it from both sides with short strokes.
cases.explain: Движение is the direct object of the transitive verb изменял (changed), so it takes the accusative case.

cases.sentence: Развязывали мешочки с хлебом и оттыкали кувшинчики с ___.
cases.translation: They untied little sacks of bread and uncorked small jugs of kvass.
cases.explain: The preposition с (with) governs the instrumental case.

cases.sentence: Наступала блаженная медленная прогулка с рукой на ___.
cases.translation: Then followed a blissful, slow walk with a hand resting on the scythe.
cases.explain: The preposition на (on) governs the prepositional case here, indicating where the hand rested.

reading.ru: После завтрака Левин попал в ряд уже не на прежнее место, а между шутником-стариком, который пригласил его в соседи, и молодым мужиком, с осени только женатым и пошедшим косить первое лето.
reading.question: Where did Levin end up in the mowing line after breakfast?
options: Between a joking old man and a young recently-married peasant
At the very front, leading the row
Next to his brother Sergei Ivanovich
reading.correct: Between a joking old man and a young recently-married peasant
reading.explain: The text says he took a place between a joking old man and a young peasant married since autumn.

reading.question: Who walked behind Levin?
reading.explain: The text says young Mishka walked behind Levin.

reading.ru: В самый жар казьба показалась ему не так трудна.
reading.question: How did the mowing feel to Levin in the greatest heat?
options: Easier than in the morning cold
reading.explain: The text says in the very heat the mowing seemed not so hard to him.

reading.question: How does the text describe the moments when Levin's mind went blank while mowing?
reading.explain: The text says 'Это были счастливые минуты' (These were happy minutes).

reading.ru: И тотчас после этого наступала блаженная медленная прогулка с рукой на косе, во время которой можно было отереть ливший пот, вздохнуть полную грудью и оглядеть всю тянущуюся вереницу косцов и то, что делалось вокруг, в лесу и в поле.
reading.question: What followed the exertion of mowing to the river?
options: A blissful, slow walk back with a hand resting on the scythe, wiping off sweat and looking around
An immediate second row without rest
reading.correct: A blissful, slow walk back with a hand resting on the scythe, wiping off sweat and looking around
reading.explain: The text describes a blissful slow walk with a hand on the scythe, during which he could wipe sweat and look around.

reading.ru: Трудно было только тогда, когда надо было прекращать это сделавшееся бессознательным движение и думать, когда надо было окашивать кочку или невыполненный щавельник.
reading.question: When did the work become difficult again?
options: When he had to stop the unconscious movement and think, such as when mowing around a hummock
reading.correct: When he had to stop the unconscious movement and think, such as when mowing around a hummock
reading.explain: The text says it was hard only when he had to stop the unconscious movement and think, as when mowing around a hummock.

reading.ru: То он срывал кочеток, съедал его или угощал Левина, то отбрасывал носком косы в ветку, то оглядывал гнездышко перепелины, из которого из-под самой косы вылетала самка, то ловил козюлю, попавшуюся на пути, и, как вилкой подняв ее косой, показывал Левину и отбрасывал.
reading.question: What small things did the old man notice and do while mowing?
options: He picked mushrooms or berries to eat or share, spotted a quail's nest, and caught a snake to show Levin
He argued with the other peasants
reading.correct: He picked mushrooms or berries to eat or share, spotted a quail's nest, and caught a snake to show Levin
reading.explain: The text describes him picking things to eat or offer Levin, noticing a quail's nest, and catching a snake to show Levin.

reading.ru: Если бы спросили его, сколько времени он косил, он сказал бы, что полчаса.
reading.question: If asked how long he had been mowing, what would Levin have guessed?
reading.explain: The text says if asked, he would have said half an hour, though much more time had passed.

reading.question: What did the old man announce decisively?
options: That it was time to eat dinner
That it was time to stop for the day
reading.correct: That it was time to eat dinner
reading.explain: The old man says decisively, '«Ну, барин, обедать!»' (Time to dine, master!).

reading.ru: Всякое стеснение пред барином уже давно исчезло.
reading.question: How had the peasants' attitude toward Levin (the barin) changed by this point?
options: All awkwardness/shyness before him had long since disappeared
They had become hostile toward him
reading.correct: All awkwardness/shyness before him had long since disappeared
reading.explain: The text says all constraint before the master had long since vanished.

reading.ru: Старик накрошил в чашку хлеба, размял его стеблем ложки, налил воды из брусницы, еще разрезал хлеба и, посыпав солью, стал на восток молиться.
reading.question: What did the old man do before eating?
options: He prepared his food (bread soaked in water and salted) and then prayed facing east
He washed in the river first
He gave all his food to the children
He refused to eat until Levin did
reading.correct: He prepared his food (bread soaked in water and salted) and then prayed facing east
reading.explain: The text describes him crumbling bread, adding water and salt, then standing to pray facing east.

reading.ru: Когда старик опять встал, помолился и лег тут же под кустом, положив себе под изголовье травы, Левин сделал то же, и, несмотря на липких, упорных на солнце мух и козявок, щекотавших его потное лицо и тело, заснул тотчас же и проснулся только когда солнце зашло на другую сторону куста и стало доставать его.
reading.question: What did Levin do after the old man lay down to rest under the bush?
options: He did the same and fell asleep at once
He went back to the house
reading.correct: He did the same and fell asleep at once
reading.explain: The text says Levin did the same, and despite the flies and midges, fell asleep immediately.

reading.ru: Огромное пространство луга было скошено и блестело особенным новым блеском со своими уже пахнущими рядами на вечерних косых лучах солнца.
reading.question: What did Levin see when he woke up and looked at the meadow?
options: A huge expanse already mown, gleaming with a new fragrance in the evening light
The meadow completely untouched, as before
The old man gone, replaced by strangers
reading.correct: A huge expanse already mown, gleaming with a new fragrance in the evening light
reading.explain: The text says an enormous space of the meadow was already mown and shone with a new gleam in the slanting evening sun.

reading.ru: Нескошенными оставались углы с короткими рядами.
reading.question: What parts of the large meadow remained unmown?
options: Only the areas near the river
reading.explain: The text says only the corners with short rows remained unmown.

reading.ru: Во время полдника, когда опять сели и курящие закурили, старик объявил ребятам, что Машкин верх скосить, водка будет.
reading.question: What did the old man announce during the mid-afternoon rest?
options: That if they mowed Mashkin Verkh too, there would be vodka
That they should stop for the day
reading.correct: That if they mowed Mashkin Verkh too, there would be vodka
reading.explain: The old man declared to the lads that if they mowed Mashkin Verkh, there would be vodka.

reading.ru: «Ну, ребята, держись!» — сказал Тит, и почти рысью пошел передом.
reading.question: How did Tit lead the way to Mashkin Verkh?
options: Nearly at a trot, urging the others to keep up
By letting the old man lead instead
reading.correct: Nearly at a trot, urging the others to keep up
reading.explain: Tit said 'Hold on, lads!' and went ahead almost at a trot.

reading.ru: Трава была по пояс в середине лощины и нежная, и мягкая, лопушистая, кое-где по лесу пестреющая Иваном да Марией.
reading.question: Who led the mowers into the ravine after a brief discussion about direction?
options: Prokhor Yermilin, a huge, swarthy, well-known mower
reading.correct: Prokhor Yermilin, a huge, swarthy, well-known mower
reading.explain: The text names Prokhor Yermilin, another well-known mower, a huge dark-complexioned peasant, as going ahead.

reading.question: What was difficult about mowing in the ravine, even though the wet grass itself was easy to cut?
options: Climbing up and down the steep slopes of the ravine
reading.correct: Climbing up and down the steep slopes of the ravine
reading.explain: The text says it was easy to mow the wet grass, but difficult to climb up and down the steep slopes of the ravine.
